part.name: STM32H723ZGTx
part.description: STMicroelectronics Arm Cortex-M7 MCU, 1024KB flash, 564KB RAM, 550 MHz, 1.62-3.6V, 114 GPIO, LQFP144

pins.name: VBAT
pins.note: Backup supply. Tying it to the main rail is normal; floating it is not.

pins.name: NRST
pins.note: Reset must be strapped or driven. A floating reset is the classic intermittent-boot fault.

pins.name: VSSA
pins.note: Analog return. Kept as its own domain because tying it to digital ground is a decision, not a default.

pins.name: VCAP
pins.note: Internal-regulator output brought out only so a capacitor can be hung on it.

pins.name: VCAP
pins.note: Internal-regulator output brought out only so a capacitor can be hung on it.

pins.name: BOOT0
pins.note: Sampled at reset. It decides how the part comes up, so it must be strapped deliberately.

companions.rationale: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.
A capacitor on reset stretches the release past the supply's rise and keeps noise off the pin.
Reset needs a defined idle level. Many parts have an internal pull-up, which is why this is a warning rather than an error.

rules.rationale: A supply or return pin that reaches no net means the part is unpowered.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.
Strapping pins are sampled once at reset. Floating, they decide the boot mode at random and the part comes up differently between boards.
